story_text.value:
StarSkirmish: Hillclimb is a long horizon implementation of the StarCraft: Broodwar based LLM benchmark that I released last week.

Each LLM writes a Protoss bot in C++ against BWAPI, played on OpenBW. They must climb five tiers of Protoss opponents, from scripted demo bots up to top rated human written bots like Stardust and PurpleWave.

The StarSkirmish bench restricted LLMs to 1 hour of wall clock time for reasoning. With Hillclimb there is no fixed time limit.

GPT-6 Astra and Claude 5.5 Opus both benefit from substantially longer reasoning periods than 1 hour and so this format is a more realistic depiction of their abilities

title.value: Show HN: GPT-6 Astra and Claude 5.5 Opus race to create the best StarCraft bot

story_text.value:
I'm a small indie developer, I've made a mac app called Sidekins

It is a small desktop character that you can design yourself(I call it a Kin/Sidekin) and lives around your screen and peeps from the side when not in use.

It is a very social app, you can add your friends and chat with them using your Kin. It is an AI agent so you can ask in the main chat to delivery some message to your friend and it creates the message you want and animation using your Kin and goes to your friends desktop and speaks/act out your message.

You can also ask it to help you "guide" through your mac, or any app, it moves and points around telling you how things work. There is also a "do" mode, this actually does things for you on your mac, like play this song on Spotify or add an iPhone 16 to my amazon cart.

you can see the demos here on the website on what and how it does things : www.sidekins.com

Currently, it works on Mac with apple silicon, and has 300 free messages.

Try it out, and connect with me on the app: @18kushaljain

title.value: Show HN: Sidekins – a Mac companion that visits friends and does your work

story_text.value:
Outis fights spam generating and sending a fake "user unknown" bounce for an email you received, so the sender believes your address does not exist.

Of course this isn't a novel idea, I created a similar program back in 1998–1999 (actually, with a slightly different purpose), but I decided to revive it because it should work quite well with the recent trend of automated emails generated by AI, where the sender might expect a reply; it helps remove your email address from their list.

I don't have strong evidence about its effectiveness, but I'm testing it for few weeks and the spam noise seems to be reduced; I don't receive similar or followup emails any more.

Any idea on how to improve it? :)

story_text.value:
I built this because with latest coding models, Claude goes into deep-work mode with obscure commands so that I never know anymore what it's up to.

This is a mod (a plugin using Claude Code's new function hooks) that draws one line above the prompt:

- the current step, using the description Claude writes for each shell command (git bisect run npx vitest … → "Find the commit that broke fixed-amount coupons"), with a timer

- a row per background agent, kept after the turn ends

- ▸ expands into the turn's history, with outcomes and durations

It reads the model's stream, tool calls and permission requests, and doesn't change anything Claude does. No network, no telemetry, MIT.

Happy to answer questions about this mod or the mod building experience!

title.value: Show HN: What's Agent Doing – a Claude Code UI mod that explains each step

story_text.value:
Hello there,

I've built Fougere, a Typescript-first framework you can add to an existing app, or run on its own.

It's alpha for now, and the docs are full of AI slop. The code was written with heavy help from Claude — I guided it in every way I could — and hasn't been fully reviewed yet, but the ideas are there.

In Fougere, business logic is at the center of everything.

Once the domain code is written, everything else is derived from it — you don't write it: validation, REST, GraphQL, the database tables, etc. You can also split the application in many parts without changing one line in businness code (only one line in config). In fact, I really like this way of building apps, but I'm a bit alone with it, and I'd like your take on these patterns. Is it useful to you? Do you use this kind of framework? Is there something to add, to change, or that seems unclear or useless? Any advice or feedback is greatly appreciated!

Thanks!

story_text.value:
I made dishlist, an iPhone app that is available in the App Store. It is a restaurant recommendation app, like Yelp and Beli. It is different because it is built around things on the menu. Playlists let us organize our favorite songs. What if we did that with our favorite things on the menu?

I've indexed every menu item at 109 places in Dogpatch, Potrero Hill, and Mission Bay (4,332 dishes and 5,285 drinks). You can search for the types of things you like and you can even search by ingredient. You can rank your favorite Breakfast Burritos, Boba, or whatever else you like.

Website

https://dishlist.com

Video

https://dishlist.com/demo

story_text.value:
Why I thought this might be interesting for HN – there is a dynamic-code-insertion feature. When you reach 2000 units, you will get an input field where you can describe whatever behavior or command for your swarm and an LLM will create a code that will perform it. Can be something as simple as ‘make a heart’ or more complex, like ‘turn blue when enemies are nearby’. Or describing some kiting strategies.

More of an early demo, but I'm curious what people think about the concept.
